usage: This is the standard, direct way to apologize for a mistake in Cairo, used across all social classes. The form changes based on the gender of the speaker, not the listener. While suitable for both formal and casual situations, close friends often use 'ma3lesh' for minor bumps or issues.

variants.label: feminine speaker
variants.note: Use this if you are a woman apologizing.

variants.label: plural speaker
variants.note: Use this when apologizing on behalf of a group or couple.

variants.label: deep apology / soothing
variants.note: Literally 'your right is upon me', used to deeply apologize and appease someone who is upset.

variants.label: casual / minor mistake
variants.note: Used for minor accidents or to express sympathy, but can sound dismissive if used for a major offense.

responses.english: No worries / Don't worry about it
It's completely normal / No problem at all

examples.english: I'm sorry that I'm late (to a man).
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to.

examples.arabic: أَنَا آسِف، مِش هَقْدَر أَاجِي النَّهَارْدَة.
examples.transliteration: ana aasef, mesh ha2dar aagy el naharda.
examples.english: I'm sorry, I won't be able to come today.
